# Agent N's Hermes News — Executive Summary

Coverage date: 2026-09-23 · Published: 2026-09-24

Executive Summary

The week belongs to Hermes Desktop's Bot Screen launch: agents' sessions now stream live on your desktop, and you can interactively take over the agent's machine via live desktop passthrough. Official announcements from @NousResearch and @Teknium (the companion post hit 173k views and 1.1k+ likes) were followed by rapid distribution of @tonbistudio's walkthrough — with community reactions like "Finallllly!" confirming this was the most long-awaited feature in recent memory.

On the research side, coverage centered on the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: how Hermes drives the unmodified official Claude Code CLI, and how its keyless authentication keeps credentials entirely with the official CLI via one-time login. Meanwhile, Hermes Agent v0.21.4 adds machine-readable JSONL output for scripters, @rlaope shipped a wave of OMH and Jev tooling, and the broader agent-runtime ecosystem (with AgentProto v0.20.0 and Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0) is increasingly treating Hermes as a first-class integration target.

Releases

  • Hermes Desktop — Bot Screen + Live Desktop Passthrough (headline launch): watch agent sessions stream in real time and interactively take over the agent's machine. Announced by @NousResearch, with @Teknium launching live desktop passthrough in the companion post (173k views, 1.1k+ likes).
  • Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (released 21 September 2026): adds a --format stream-json flag emitting structured JSONL. An immediate upgrade win for anyone scripting against the CLI — the project's steady cadence continues with a focus on automation-friendly, machine-readable output.
  • AgentProto v0.20.0 (22 September 2026): a new open-source TypeScript agent runtime that already lists Hermes among its integrated agents. Worth tracking for interoperability with your Hermes setups.
  • Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: hardens MCP security with per-invocation session scoping — a pattern directly relevant to Hermes's own MCP discovery and integration configuration.

Community

  • Bot Screen launch reception: Official onboarding moved fast — @NousResearch distributed @tonbistudio's walkthrough (44k views) and @Teknium amplified the guide video. Reactions like "Finallllly!" signal strong demand finally met.
  • Builder ecosystem momentum: @rlaope shipped oh-my-hermes (OMH) support for Jev-Skills, Model Routing, aliases, and plugins, plus the open-source jeval tool for Jev evaluation and visualization — a material expansion of the community plugin ecosystem and better tooling for evaluating Jev model outputs.
  • Core-team support stayed hands-on: @Teknium rebutted a plugin cache-bug claim by demanding a reproducible issue path, confirmed a quick community-reported fix, and clarified the new tooling is Nous-built rather than Anthropic's. @NousResearch advised a user on accessing Hermes via iMessage with any model.
  • Sentiment watch: a widely shared take that Claude Opus 5.5 (GA'd the day before coverage) is impressive but Claude Code lags — read as quiet confidence in Hermes Agent as the driver layer.

Tips & Tutorials

  • Getting started with Bot Screen: follow @tonbistudio's walkthrough (distributed via @NousResearch and amplified by @Teknium) for the fastest path from install to watching — and taking over — live agent sessions.
  • Running Hermes on top of Claude: two deep-dives on the Hermes-Claude plugin cover the pipeline architecture that lets Hermes drive the unmodified official Claude Code CLI, plus a security-focused guide to its keyless authentication flow — credentials stay entirely with the official CLI via one-time login. Directly actionable if you're running or evaluating the plugin.
  • Scripting against the CLI: upgrade to Hermes Agent v0.21.4 and use --format stream-json to consume structured JSONL events instead of parsing free-form terminal output.
  • Quick access tip: per @NousResearch, you can reach Hermes via iMessage with any model — no extra setup required for casual use.

entry.title: It's time! You can now access the same machine your Hermes Agent does visually and interactively wit...
entry.summary: Teknium announces live desktop passthrough: users can now visually and interactively access the same machine their Hermes Agent operates on, supported on every remote gateway.

entry.title: Hermes Claude CLI: The Pipeline Behind The Plugin
entry.summary: Deep-dive on the pipeline powering the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: Hermes talks to a plugin that drives the unmodified official Claude Code executable, with conversation flowing as native stream-json while Hermes retains its own loop, tools, approvals and compaction. No forked CLI or patched binary is used. Every request spawns a fresh claude process in a private temp directory with native tools and skills disabled so Hermes controls the tool inventory. An admission relay forwards exactly one upstream request per turn, rejecting native retry attempts locally to keep billing honest. Version requirements: Hermes 0.21.4+ and the qualified native Claude Code 2.1.263.

entry.title: Hermes Agent Stream JSON Output: New in v0.21.4
entry.summary: Covers Hermes Agent v0.21.4 (tagged v2026.9.21, released 21 September 2026), which adds a --format stream-json CLI flag emitting structured JSONL, one JSON object per line, enabling reliable parsing by scripts and pipelines. Upgrade paths include hermes update for git installs, the installer one-liner, or the nousresearch/hermes-agent:v2026.9.21 Docker image. The same release rolls up roughly 1,812 merged PRs, including skills auto-load and configurable MCP discovery concurrency. The feature is free and built into the open-source agent.

entry.title:
OMH now supports Jev-Skils and Model Routing.
• Jev models and aliases • Jev skills and plugins ...
entry.summary: rlaope announces that oh-my-hermes (OMH) now supports Jev-Skills and Model Routing, listing features including Jev models and aliases, skills and plugins, Jev-powered workflow routing, fast decisions for skills, models, agents, memory, and MCP, plugin status and credential checks, plus routing benchmarks and answer scoring.

entry.title: Hermes-Claude Auth: How Login Works (No API Key)
entry.summary: Explains authentication for the Hermes-Claude subscription plugin: credentials remain entirely with the official Claude Code CLI via a one-time claude auth login flow; the plugin never opens, copies, refreshes or prints credential files, and no API key is required or sent anywhere in the flow. The plugin actively rejects inherited API-key, custom-endpoint and cloud override variables, naming conflicting variables without exposing their values. Status checks like claude auth status read the local credential store locally in roughly 0.3s. Separated setups can use CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR and CLAUDE_SUBSCRIPTION_DIRECTSDK_CONFIG_DIR to point at a dedicated CLI-managed config directory.

entry.title: AgentProto Review: New Open Agent Runtime (2026)
entry.summary: Review of AgentProto, an open-source agentic runtime in TypeScript released as v0.20.0 on 22 September 2026. It provides one interface to start, message, watch and stop coding agents in the background with quality gates before work lands. Its README claims integration with 14 agents including Claude Code, Codex, Gemini, Hermes, opencode and Mastra. The project is Apache-2.0 licensed and free, with users paying only for underlying model usage. The reviewer notes it is very early: single-digit GitHub stars, alpha-level Tier 2 components, and a verdict of interesting architecture but early-adopters-only.

entry.title: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0: What Changed
entry.summary: Overview of Microsoft Agent Framework 1.19.0, tagged on GitHub on 18 September 2026. Key changes center on MCP security: sessions are scoped per invocation with requests authenticated against the correct invocation identity, origin and ownership. Skill archives are now ZIP-only with digest verification, and ambiguous MCP configuration matches are rejected. New vector-store connectors were added for MongoDB, Azure DocumentDB and Azure Cosmos DB, plus in-memory and portable filters. The article flags breaking changes, including deprecation of the MCP sampling callback, and warns readers to review before upgrading.
